questionText: P, Q and R, when working individually, can complete a job in, respectively, 36 days, 48 days and 144 days. P, Q and R start working together. P leaves the job 12 days before completion and Q leaves the job 8 days before completion. R works from the beginning till the end of the job. Determine the total number of days taken to complete the job.
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(36, 48, 144) = 144\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = \frac{144}{36} = 4$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Q} = \frac{144}{48} = 3$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = \frac{144}{144} = 1$$
$$\text{Let the total time taken be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$4(T - 12) + 3(T - 8) + 1(T) = 144$$
$$4T - 48 + 3T - 24 + T = 144$$
$$8T - 72 = 144 \implies 8T = 216 \implies T = 27\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: Benny can do a piece of work in 24 days. Chetan and David can do the same work individually in 36 and 48 days respectively. All of them begin the work together. However, Benny leaves the work 4 days before the completion of work and Chetan leaves the work 10 days before the completion of the work. David worked till the end and completed the work. Find the number of days in which the work was completed.
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(24, 36, 48) = 144\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Benny} = \frac{144}{24} = 6$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Chetan} = \frac{144}{36} = 4$$
$$\text{Efficiency of David} = \frac{144}{48} = 3$$
$$\text{Let total time taken be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$6(T - 4) + 4(T - 10) + 3T = 144$$
$$6T - 24 + 4T - 40 + 3T = 144$$
$$13T - 64 = 144 \implies 13T = 208 \implies T = 16\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: P, Q and R can complete a work alone in 12, 15 and 20 days respectively. They started the work together. P left the work 8 days before the work was completed and Q left the work 5 days after P had left. R completed the remaining work alone. How many days will be required to complete the whole work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(12, 15, 20) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = \frac{60}{12} = 5$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Q} = \frac{60}{15} = 4$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = \frac{60}{20} = 3$$
$$\text{Let total time be } T \text{ days. P left } 8 \text{ days before completion, so P worked for } (T - 8) \text{ days.}$$
$$\text{Q left } 5 \text{ days after P, so Q worked for } (T - 8 + 5) = (T - 3) \text{ days.}$$
$$\text{R worked for all } T \text{ days.}$$
$$5(T - 8) + 4(T - 3) + 3T = 60$$
$$5T - 40 + 4T - 12 + 3T = 60$$
$$12T - 52 = 60 \implies 12T = 112 \implies T = \frac{112}{12} = \frac{28}{3}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: Aarif, Arun and Abraham can do a work in 12, 20 and 24 days, respectively. They all begin together. Aarif leaves the work 1 day, Arun 3 days and Abraham 4 days before its completion. In how many days is the work finished?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(12, 20, 24) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Aarif} = \frac{120}{12} = 10$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Arun} = \frac{120}{20} = 6$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Abraham} = \frac{120}{24} = 5$$
$$\text{Let total time be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$10(T - 1) + 6(T - 3) + 5(T - 4) = 120$$
$$10T - 10 + 6T - 18 + 5T - 20 = 120$$
$$21T - 48 = 120 \implies 21T = 168 \implies T = 8\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: A alone can do a work in 14 days. B alone can do the same work in 28 days. C alone can do the same work in 56 days. They started working together and completed the work such that B was not working on last 2 days and A did not work in last 3 days. In how many days (total) was the work completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(14, 28, 56) = 56\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{56}{14} = 4$$
$$\text{Efficiency of B} = \frac{56}{28} = 2$$
$$\text{Efficiency of C} = \frac{56}{56} = 1$$
$$\text{Let total time be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$\text{A worked for } (T - 3) \text{ days, B worked for } (T - 2) \text{ days, and C worked for } T \text{ days.}$$
$$4(T - 3) + 2(T - 2) + 1(T) = 56$$
$$4T - 12 + 2T - 4 + T = 56$$
$$7T - 16 = 56 \implies 7T = 72 \implies T = \frac{72}{7}\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IV: CONCEPT OF LEAVING THE WORK
questionText: A, B and C separately can do a piece of work in 18, 36 and 54 days respectively. They started the work together, but B and C left 5 days and 10 days respectively before the completion of the work. In how many days will the work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(18, 36, 54) = 108\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{108}{18} = 6$$
$$\text{Efficiency of B} = \frac{108}{36} = 3$$
$$\text{Efficiency of C} = \frac{108}{54} = 2$$
$$\text{Let total time taken be } T \text{ days.}$$
$$6T + 3(T - 5) + 2(T - 10) = 108$$
$$6T + 3T - 15 + 2T - 20 = 108$$
$$11T - 35 = 108 \implies 11T = 143 \implies T = 13\text{ days}$$

questionText: A can do $\frac{1}{5}$ of a piece of work in 20 days, B can do 30% of the same work in 36 days, while C can do 80% of the same work in 160 days. B and C together started and worked for x days. After x days B left the work, and A joined C and both completed the remaining work in $(x - 41)$ days. If the ratio between the work done by $(B + C)$ together to the work done by $(A + C)$ together is $19 : 6$, then what fraction of the same work can be completed by C alone in 2x days?
solution:
$$\text{Total days for A} = 20 \times 5 = 100\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days for B} = 36 \times \frac{10}{3} = 120\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days for C} = 160 \times \frac{5}{4} = 200\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(100, 120, 200) = 600\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 6,\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = 5,\quad \text{Efficiency of C} = 3$$
$$\text{Rate of }(B + C) = 5 + 3 = 8,\quad \text{Rate of }(A + C) = 6 + 3 = 9$$
$$\frac{8x}{9(x - 41)} = \frac{19}{6} \implies 48x = 171x - 7011$$
$$123x = 7011 \implies x = 57$$
$$\text{Work done by C alone in } 2x = 114\text{ days} = 114 \times 3 = 342\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Fraction} = \frac{342}{600} = \frac{57}{100}$$

questionText: Ramesh does half as much work as Parul in $\frac{4}{5}$ of the time. If together Ramesh and Parul take 24 days to complete the work, then how much time will Parul take to do it?
solution:
$$\text{Let Parul's efficiency be } P \text{ and Ramesh's efficiency be } R.$$
$$R \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{2} P \implies R = \frac{5}{8} P \implies \frac{R}{P} = \frac{5}{8}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (5 + 8) \times 24 = 13 \times 24 = 312\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Parul alone} = \frac{312}{8} = 39\text{ days}$$

questionText: Babita is 1.25 times as efficient as Deepak. Working together the duo can complete a piece of work in 40 days. In how many days can Deepak alone complete the same piece of work?
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies Babita : Deepak} = 1.25 : 1 = 5 : 4$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 5 + 4 = 9$$
$$\text{Total work} = 9 \times 40 = 360\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Deepak alone} = \frac{360}{4} = 90\text{ days}$$

questionText: Sapna is double efficient as compared to Rakesh. If they both work together on a project and complete it in 48 days, then the number of days in which Sapna alone can complete the project is:
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies Sapna : Rakesh} = 2 : 1$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 1 = 3$$
$$\text{Total work} = 3 \times 48 = 144\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Sapna alone} = \frac{144}{2} = 72\text{ days}$$

questionText: Teena does half of a task in 6 days. Later, with shyam's help, she completes the ramaining work in 4 days. Shyam alone can finish the entire work in:
solution:
$$\text{Teena can complete the whole work in } 6 \times 2 = 12\text{ days.}$$
$$\text{Teena and Shyam together can complete remaining half in 4 days } \implies \text{entire work in } 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ days.}$$
$$\frac{1}{\text{Shyam}} = \frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3 - 2}{24} = \frac{1}{24}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Shyam alone} = 24\text{ days}$$

questionText: Joy completed the school project in 15 days. How many days will Tim take to complete the same work if he is 25% more efficient than Joy?
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiency Tim : Joy} = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4$$
$$\text{Time ratio Tim : Joy} = 4 : 5$$
$$\text{Time taken by Tim} = 15 \times \frac{4}{5} = 12\text{ days}$$

questionText: Nirmal completed the school project in 45 days How many days will Amit take to complete the same work if he is 25% more efficient than Nirmal?
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiency Amit : Nirmal} = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4$$
$$\text{Time ratio Amit : Nirmal} = 4 : 5$$
$$\text{Time taken by Amit} = 45 \times \frac{4}{5} = 36\text{ days}$$

questionText: Arvind works 4 times as fast as Suresh. If Suresh can complete a work in 20 days independently, then find the number of days in which Arvind and Suresh can together finish the work.
solution:
$$\text{Efficiency of Suresh} = 1,\quad \text{Efficiency of Arvind} = 4$$
$$\text{Total work} = 1 \times 20 = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 4 + 1 = 5$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{20}{5} = 4\text{ days}$$

questionText: Tarun is twice as good as Tripti in doing a work. Together, they can complete the work in 16 days. In how many days can Tripti alone complete the same work?
solution:
$$\text{Efficiency of Tarun : Tripti} = 2 : 1$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 1 = 3$$
$$\text{Total work} = 3 \times 16 = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Tripti alone} = \frac{48}{1} = 48\text{ days}$$

questionText: P is two times efficient than Q. P is able to complete a piece of work in 40 days less than Q. Working together, the whole number of days taken by them to complete the work is: (Round off to the nearest integer)
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies } P : Q = 2 : 1 \implies \text{Time ratio } P : Q = 1 : 2$$
$$\text{Difference in time} = 2x - x = x = 40\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by P} = 40\text{ days},\quad \text{Time taken by Q} = 80\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 80\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{80}{2 + 1} = \frac{80}{3} = 26.67 \approx 27\text{ days}$$

questionText: X alone can complete a work in 18 days and Y alone can do the same work in half time of the time taken by X. Working together what part of the same work they can complete in a day?
solution:
$$\text{Time taken by X} = 18\text{ days},\quad \text{Time taken by Y} = \frac{18}{2} = 9\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Work done by X in 1 day} = \frac{1}{18}$$
$$\text{Work done by Y in 1 day} = \frac{1}{9}$$
$$\text{Work done together in 1 day} = \frac{1}{18} + \frac{1}{9} = \frac{1 + 2}{18} = \frac{3}{18} = \frac{1}{6}$$

questionText: Raj alone can complete a work in 20 days and Pratap alone can complete the same work in half of the time taken by Raj. In how many days, will both together complete $\frac{3}{5}$ part of the total work?
solution:
$$\text{Time taken by Raj} = 20\text{ days},\quad \text{Time taken by Pratap} = 10\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(20, 10) = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Raj} = 1,\quad \text{Efficiency of Pratap} = 2$$
$$\text{Required work} = \frac{3}{5} \times 20 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{12}{1 + 2} = \frac{12}{3} = 4\text{ days}$$

questionText: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 48 days. A is 4 times as efficient as B. In how many days B alone can complete the work?
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies } A : B = 4 : 1$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 4 + 1 = 5$$
$$\text{Total work} = 5 \times 48 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{240}{1} = 240\text{ days}$$

questionText: R can finish a work in 6 days if he works 10 hours a day. S can finish it in 5 days if he works 8 hours a day. If both start a work and work daily for 6 hours, the work will be finished in days.
solution:
$$\text{Total hours for R} = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Total hours for S} = 5 \times 8 = 40\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(60, 40) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = \frac{120}{60} = 2\text{ units/hour},\quad \text{Efficiency of S} = \frac{120}{40} = 3\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Combined hourly rate} = 2 + 3 = 5\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Total hours needed} = \frac{120}{5} = 24\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Days required (at 6 hours/day)} = \frac{24}{6} = 4\text{ days}$$

questionText: If 6 engineers can complete a work in 5 days and 5 skilled workers can complete the same work in 7 days, then the time taken (in days) to complete the same work by 7 engineers and 4 skilled workers will be
solution:
$$6E \times 5 = 5S \times 7 \implies 30E = 35S \implies 6E = 7S \implies \frac{E}{S} = \frac{7}{6}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 30 \times 7 = 210\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 7E + 4S = 7(7) + 4(6) = 49 + 24 = 73\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{210}{73} = 2\frac{64}{73}\text{ days}$$

questionText: To finish a work, P takes half of the number of days required by Q to finish it. If they together can finish the work in 36 days, then in how many days Q alone can finish the work?
solution:
$$\text{Time ratio } P : Q = 1 : 2 \implies \text{Efficiency ratio } P : Q = 2 : 1$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 1 = 3$$
$$\text{Total work} = 3 \times 36 = 108\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Q alone} = \frac{108}{1} = 108\text{ days}$$

questionText: A work can be done by a man and a woman in 12 days and 8 days, respectively. In how many days will the work be done by 6 men and 4 women?
solution:
$$\text{Rate of 1 man} = \frac{1}{12},\quad \text{Rate of 1 woman} = \frac{1}{8}$$
$$\text{Rate of 6 men and 4 women} = 6 \times \frac{1}{12} + 4 \times \frac{1}{8} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} = 1\text{ work/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{1}{1} = 1\text{ day}$$

questionText: If 4 men or 6 boys can finish a piece of work in 20 days, then in how many days can 6 men and 11 boys finish the same work?
solution:
$$4M = 6B \implies 2M = 3B \implies \frac{M}{B} = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 4(3) \times 20 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 6M + 11B = 6(3) + 11(2) = 18 + 22 = 40\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{240}{40} = 6\text{ days}$$

questionText: If 2 men or 4 women can build a wall in 34 days, in how many days can 6 men and 5 women build the same wall?
solution:
$$2M = 4W \implies 1M = 2W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{2}{1}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 2(2) \times 34 = 136\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 6M + 5W = 6(2) + 5(1) = 12 + 5 = 17\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{136}{17} = 8\text{ days}$$

questionText: Working 5 hours a day, A can complete a task in 8 days and working 6 hours a day, B can finish the same task in 10 days. Working 8 hours a day, they can jointly complete the task in _____.
solution:
$$\text{Total hours for A} = 5 \times 8 = 40\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Total hours for B} = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(40, 60) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{120}{40} = 3\text{ units/hour},\quad \text{Efficiency of B} = \frac{120}{60} = 2\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Combined hourly rate} = 3 + 2 = 5\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Total hours required} = \frac{120}{5} = 24\text{ hours}$$
$$\text{Days required (at 8 hours/day)} = \frac{24}{8} = 3\text{ days}$$

questionText: A alone can finish a work in 15 days. A works only for the first two days and last two days. The rest work is done by B and the work is completed in 20 days. In how many days A and B together can finish the work?
solution:
$$\text{Let total work} = 60\text{ units}.\quad \text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{60}{15} = 4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{A worked for } 2 + 2 = 4\text{ days } \implies \text{work done by A} = 4 \times 4 = 16\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 60 - 16 = 44\text{ units, completed by B in } 20 - 4 = 16\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of B} = \frac{44}{16} = \frac{11}{4}\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 4 + \frac{11}{4} = \frac{27}{4}\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{60}{27/4} = \frac{240}{27} = \frac{80}{9}\text{ days}$$

questionText: After working alone for 12 days, Reena finds that only 10 percent of the work is completed. She employs Priya who is 40 percent more efficient than Reena. How many more days will they together take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Reena completes 10% in 12 days } \implies \text{total time for Reena} = 120\text{ days.}$$
$$\text{Let total work} = 120\text{ units}.\quad \text{Efficiency of Reena} = 1$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 90\% \times 120 = 108\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of Priya} = 1 + 0.40 = 1.4$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 1 + 1.4 = 2.4$$
$$\text{Days taken for remaining work} = \frac{108}{2.4} = 45\text{ days}$$

questionText: A can do a piece of work in 25 days. After working for 5 days, he took help of B and completed the work in 8 days. If both A and B had worked together from the beginning, in how many days would they have completed the work?
solution:
$$\text{Let total work} = 100\text{ units}.\quad \text{Efficiency of A} = \frac{100}{25} = 4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Work done by A in 5 days} = 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 100 - 20 = 80\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of }(A + B) = \frac{80}{8} = 10\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken together from beginning} = \frac{100}{10} = 10\text{ days}$$

questionText: Naman does half of the work as Gagan in $\frac{4}{5}$ time. If together they take 16 days to complete a piece of work, then how long will Gagan take to complete the work?
solution:
$$\text{Let Gagan's efficiency be } G \text{ and Naman's efficiency be } N.$$
$$N \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{2} G \implies N = \frac{5}{8} G \implies \frac{N}{G} = \frac{5}{8}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (5 + 8) \times 16 = 13 \times 16 = 208\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Gagan alone} = \frac{208}{8} = 26\text{ days}$$

questionText: P can do one-fourth piece of some work in 18 days. She completed 37.5% of that work and left it. Q completed the remaining work in 40 days. Working together they will complete $\frac{17}{48}$ part of the same work in:
solution:
$$\text{Total days for P} = 18 \times 4 = 72\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 100\% - 37.5\% = 62.5\% = \frac{5}{8}$$
$$\text{Total days for Q} = 40 \times \frac{8}{5} = 64\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(72, 64) = 576\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of P} = \frac{576}{72} = 8,\quad \text{Efficiency of Q} = \frac{576}{64} = 9$$
$$\text{Work to complete} = \frac{17}{48} \times 576 = 17 \times 12 = 204\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{204}{8 + 9} = \frac{204}{17} = 12\text{ days}$$

questionText: To do a certain work, efficiencies of A and B are in the ratio $7 : 5$. Working together, they can complete the work in $17\frac{1}{2}$ days. In how many days, will B alone complete 50% of the same work?
solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies of A and B} = 7 : 5$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 7 + 5 = 12$$
$$\text{Total work} = 12 \times 17.5 = 210\text{ units}$$
$$\text{50% of the work} = \frac{210}{2} = 105\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{105}{5} = 21\text{ days}$$

questionText: Amita can build a room in the same amount of time that Bina and Sita working together can build. If Amita and Bina together could do it in 25 days and Sita alone in 35 days, then how many days are required for Bina alone to do the same work?
solution:
$$\text{Given: } E_A = E_B + E_S$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(25, 35) = 175\text{ units}$$
$$E_A + E_B = \frac{175}{25} = 7,\quad E_S = \frac{175}{35} = 5$$
$$E_A + E_B + E_S = 7 + 5 = 12$$
$$\text{Since } E_A = E_B + E_S, \text{ we have } 2E_A = 12 \implies E_A = 6$$
$$E_B = 7 - 6 = 1$$
$$\text{Time taken by Bina alone} = \frac{175}{1} = 175\text{ days}$$

questionText: Robert takes twice as much time as Tom and thrice as much time as Jeorge to complete a work. If working together, they can complete it in 23 hours, then find the time that Tom will take to complete the work.
solution:
$$\text{Time ratio } T_R : T_T : T_J = 6 : 3 : 2 \implies \text{Efficiency ratio } E_R : E_T : E_J = 1 : 2 : 3$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6$$
$$\text{Total work} = 6 \times 23 = 138\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by Tom} = \frac{138}{2} = 69\text{ hours}$$

questionText: A takes twice as much time as B and thrice as much time as C to finalise a task. Working together, they can complete the task in 8 days. The time (in days) taken by A, B and C, respectively, to complete the task is:
solution:
$$\text{Time ratio } T_A : T_B : T_C = 6 : 3 : 2 \implies \text{Efficiency ratio } E_A : E_B : E_C = 1 : 2 : 3$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6$$
$$\text{Total work} = 6 \times 8 = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A} = \frac{48}{1} = 48\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B} = \frac{48}{2} = 24\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by C} = \frac{48}{3} = 16\text{ days}$$

questionText: A and B can do a piece of work in 18 days. B and C together can do it in 30 days. If A is twice as efficient as C then in how many days can B alone do the work?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(18, 30) = 90\text{ units}$$
$$A + B = \frac{90}{18} = 5,\quad B + C = \frac{90}{30} = 3$$
$$(A + B) - (B + C) = A - C = 5 - 3 = 2$$
$$\text{Given } A = 2C \implies 2C - C = C = 2$$
$$B = 3 - C = 3 - 2 = 1$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{90}{1} = 90\text{ days}$$

questionText: The ratio of work efficiency of A, B and C is $2 : 5 : 3$. Working together, they can complete a work in 27 days. In how many days will B and C together complete $\frac{4}{9}$ parts of the work?
solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies of A, B, C} = 2 : 5 : 3$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 5 + 3 = 10$$
$$\text{Total work} = 10 \times 27 = 270\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required work} = \frac{4}{9} \times 270 = 120\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Combined rate of B and C} = 5 + 3 = 8$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{120}{8} = 15\text{ days}$$

questionText: The ratio of work efficiency of A, B and C is $2 : 3 : 5$. Working together, they can complete a work in 6 days. In how many days will A complete 20% of the work?
solution:
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10$$
$$\text{Total work} = 10 \times 6 = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{20% of work} = \frac{20}{100} \times 60 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of A} = 2$$
$$\text{Time taken by A} = \frac{12}{2} = 6\text{ days}$$

questionText: A can do a certain piece of work in 2.4 times the number of days in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together can do the same piece of work in 27 days and C alone can do it in 75 days, then how many days will B take to do this piece of work alone?
solution:
$$\frac{T_A}{T_{B+C}} = 2.4 = \frac{12}{5} \implies \frac{E_A}{E_{B+C}} = \frac{5}{12} \implies \frac{E_A}{E_A + E_B + E_C} = \frac{5}{17}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(27, 75) = 675\text{ units}$$
$$E_A + E_B = \frac{675}{27} = 25,\quad E_C = \frac{675}{75} = 9$$
$$E_A + E_B + E_C = 25 + 9 = 34$$
$$E_A = 34 \times \frac{5}{17} = 10$$
$$E_B = 25 - 10 = 15$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{675}{15} = 45\text{ days}$$

questionText: A & B can do a piece of work in 10 days. B and C can do the same work in 15 days. If A is twice as good a workman as C, find in what time B alone can do the work (in days).
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$A + B = \frac{30}{10} = 3,\quad B + C = \frac{30}{15} = 2$$
$$(A + B) - (B + C) = A - C = 3 - 2 = 1$$
$$\text{Since } A = 2C \implies 2C - C = C = 1$$
$$B = 2 - C = 2 - 1 = 1$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{30}{1} = 30\text{ days}$$

questionText: A can do a certain piece of work in 1.5 times the number of days in which B and C together can do it. If A and B together can do the same piece of work in 30 days and C alone can do it in 120 days, then how many days will B take to do this piece of work alone?
solution:
$$\frac{T_A}{T_{B+C}} = 1.5 = \frac{3}{2} \implies \frac{E_A}{E_{B+C}} = \frac{2}{3} \implies \frac{E_A}{E_A + E_B + E_C} = \frac{2}{5}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 120) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$E_A + E_B = \frac{120}{30} = 4,\quad E_C = \frac{120}{120} = 1$$
$$E_A + E_B + E_C = 4 + 1 = 5$$
$$E_A = 5 \times \frac{2}{5} = 2$$
$$E_B = 4 - 2 = 2$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{120}{2} = 60\text{ days}$$

questionText: To do a certain task X would take 3 times as long as Y and Z together; and Z would takes 4 times as long as Y and X together. Three of them together can complete the task in 10 days. How much time is taken by X and Z to complete the task?
solution:
$$\frac{E_X}{E_{Y+Z}} = \frac{1}{3} \implies E_X = \frac{1}{4}(E_X + E_Y + E_Z)$$
$$\frac{E_Z}{E_{X+Y}} = \frac{1}{4} \implies E_Z = \frac{1}{5}(E_X + E_Y + E_Z)$$
$$\text{Let total efficiency } E = 20.$$
$$E_X = \frac{20}{4} = 5,\quad E_Z = \frac{20}{5} = 4$$
$$E_X + E_Z = 5 + 4 = 9$$
$$\text{Total work} = 20 \times 10 = 200\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by X and Z together} = \frac{200}{9} = 22\frac{2}{9}\text{ days}$$

questionText: A alone can do 2/5 of a work in 12 days. B is 25 percent more efficient than A. C alone can do the same work in 12 days less than B. D is 25 percent less efficient than C. If they all work together, then the work will be completed in how many days?
solution:
$$\text{Time for A} = 12 \times \frac{5}{2} = 30\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time for B} = \frac{30}{1.25} = 24\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time for C} = 24 - 12 = 12\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time for D} = \frac{12}{0.75} = 16\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 24, 12, 16) = 240\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = 8,\quad E_B = 10,\quad E_C = 20,\quad E_D = 15$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 8 + 10 + 20 + 15 = 53$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{240}{53}\text{ days}$$

questionText: To do a certain work, A is 40% more efficient than B. Working together, they can do the same work in 15 days. A started the work and left after 15 days. B and C together completed the remaining work in next 10 days. C alone can do one third of the original work in:
solution:
$$\frac{E_A}{E_B} = \frac{140}{100} = \frac{7}{5}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (7 + 5) \times 15 = 12 \times 15 = 180\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by A in 15 days} = 7 \times 15 = 105\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 180 - 105 = 75\text{ units}$$
$$E_B + E_C = \frac{75}{10} = 7.5 \implies 5 + E_C = 7.5 \implies E_C = 2.5$$
$$\text{One-third of total work} = \frac{180}{3} = 60\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by C alone} = \frac{60}{2.5} = 24\text{ days}$$

questionText: A can complete a work in $11\frac{1}{2}$ days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 50% as efficient as B. Working together A, B and C will complete the same work
solution:
$$\text{Time for A} = \frac{23}{2}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Let } E_A = 4. \quad \text{Total work} = 4 \times \frac{23}{2} = 46\text{ units}$$
$$E_B = 1.25 \times 4 = 5$$
$$E_C = 0.50 \times 5 = 2.5$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 4 + 5 + 2.5 = 11.5 = \frac{23}{2}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{46}{23/2} = 4\text{ days}$$

questionText: A does a work in 15 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 40% more efficient than B. A and C work together for 3 days and then C leaves. A and B together complete the remaining work:
solution:
$$\text{Let } E_A = 20. \quad \text{Total work} = 20 \times 15 = 300\text{ units}$$
$$E_B = 1.25 \times 20 = 25$$
$$E_C = 1.40 \times 25 = 35$$
$$\text{Work done by A and C in 3 days} = (20 + 35) \times 3 = 165\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 300 - 165 = 135\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of }(A + B) = 20 + 25 = 45$$
$$\text{Time taken by A and B} = \frac{135}{45} = 3\text{ days}$$

questionText: A can complete a work in 40 days. B is 25% more efficient than A and C is 28% more efficient than B. They work together for 5 days. How many days will B alone take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Let } E_A = 20. \quad \text{Total work} = 20 \times 40 = 800\text{ units}$$
$$E_B = 1.25 \times 20 = 25$$
$$E_C = 1.28 \times 25 = 32$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 20 + 25 + 32 = 77$$
$$\text{Work done in 5 days} = 77 \times 5 = 385\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 800 - 385 = 415\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{415}{25} = \frac{83}{5} = 16\frac{3}{5}\text{ days}$$

questionText: To complete a certain work, X is 40% more efficient than Y and Z is 40% less efficient than Y. Working together, they can complete the work in 21 days. Y and Z worked together for 35 days. In how many days will X alone complete the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Let } E_Y = 10 \implies E_X = 14,\quad E_Z = 6$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency} = 14 + 10 + 6 = 30$$
$$\text{Total work} = 30 \times 21 = 630\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by Y and Z in 35 days} = (10 + 6) \times 35 = 16 \times 35 = 560\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 630 - 560 = 70\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by X alone} = \frac{70}{14} = 5\text{ days}$$

questionText: A's efficiency is twice that of B's. A can work only for 8 hours a day while B can work for 12 hours a day. If A can finish a work in 12 days, in how many days can B finish the same work?
solution:
$$\text{Hourly efficiency ratio } A : B = 2 : 1$$
$$\text{Daily work of A} = 2 \times 8 = 16\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 16 \times 12 = 192\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Daily work of B} = 1 \times 12 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Days taken by B} = \frac{192}{12} = 16\text{ days}$$

questionText: P and Q can do a job in 24 days, Q and R can do it in 30 days, while P and R can do it in 40 days. X is four times as efficient as P, Y is half as efficient as Q, and Z is 2.5 times as efficient as R. Determine the number of days required to complete the same job if X, Y and Z work together.
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(24, 30, 40) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$P + Q = 5,\quad Q + R = 4,\quad P + R = 3$$
$$2(P + Q + R) = 12 \implies P + Q + R = 6$$
$$P = 6 - 4 = 2,\quad Q = 6 - 3 = 3,\quad R = 6 - 5 = 1$$
$$X = 4P = 8,\quad Y = 0.5Q = 1.5,\quad Z = 2.5R = 2.5$$
$$\text{Combined efficiency of } X + Y + Z = 8 + 1.5 + 2.5 = 12$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{120}{12} = 10\text{ days}$$

questionText: A, B and C can finish a work in 15 days working alternately in the same order. The efficiency of A is the same as that of B, and the efficiency of C is equal to that of A. In how many days will the work be finished if they work alternately in the order C, A and B?
solution:
$$\text{Given that } E_A = E_B = E_C.$$
$$\text{Since all three individuals have identical efficiencies, any permutation of their alternate order will yield identical daily progress.}$$
$$\text{Therefore, working alternately in the order C, A, B will take the exact same } 15\text{ days.}$$

questionText: Abha and Anuj working together completed a job in $\frac{40}{9}$ days. If Abha had worked twice as efficiently as she actually did and Anuj had worked $\frac{1}{3}$ of his actual efficiency, then the work would have been completed in $\frac{60}{17}$ days. Find the time Abha would take to complete the work alone.
solution:
$$\text{Let Abha's rate be } A \text{ and Anuj's rate be } B.$$
$$A + B = \frac{9}{40} W$$
$$2A + \frac{1}{3}B = \frac{17}{60} W$$
$$\text{Multiplying first equation by } \frac{1}{3}: \quad \frac{1}{3}A + \frac{1}{3}B = \frac{3}{40} W$$
$$\text{Subtracting: } \left(2 - \frac{1}{3}\right)A = \frac{17}{60} - \frac{3}{40}$$
$$\frac{5}{3} A = \frac{34 - 9}{120} = \frac{25}{120} = \frac{5}{24}$$
$$A = \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{5}{24} = \frac{1}{8} W$$
$$\text{Time taken by Abha alone} = 8\text{ days}$$

questionText: A, B and C together can complete a work in $x$, 30 and 45 days, respectively. B and C worked together for 6 days. The remaining work was completed by A alone in 12 days. The value of $x$ is:
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(30, 45) = 90\text{ units}$$
$$E_B = \frac{90}{30} = 3,\quad E_C = \frac{90}{45} = 2$$
$$\text{Work done by B and C in 6 days} = (3 + 2) \times 6 = 30\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 90 - 30 = 60\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = \frac{60}{12} = 5\text{ units/day}$$
$$x = \frac{90}{5} = 18\text{ days}$$

questionText: 55 Workers can finish a work in 16 days. For finishing the same work in 10 days, how many more workers are required?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 55 \times 16 = 880\text{ worker-days}$$
$$\text{Total workers required for 10 days} = \frac{880}{10} = 88$$
$$\text{Additional workers required} = 88 - 55 = 33$$

questionText: 47 masons can dig a 35 m long trench in one day. How many masons should be employed for digging a 105m long trench of the same type in one day?
solution:
$$\frac{M_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2}{W_2} \implies \frac{47}{35} = \frac{M_2}{105}$$
$$M_2 = \frac{47 \times 105}{35} = 47 \times 3 = 141\text{ masons}$$

questionText: If 7 men working 8 hours a day for 5 day's can complete a work, then how many men are required to complete the same work if they work 10 hours a day for 7 days?
solution:
$$M_1 D_1 H_1 = M_2 D_2 H_2$$
$$7 \times 5 \times 8 = M_2 \times 7 \times 10$$
$$280 = 70 M_2 \implies M_2 = \frac{280}{70} = 4\text{ men}$$

questionText: 16 men can dig a ditch 24 m long in 18 days, working 6 hours a day. How many more men should be engaged to dig a similar ditch 42 m long in 9 days, each man now working 12 hours per day?
solution:
$$\frac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$$
$$\frac{16 \times 18 \times 6}{24} = \frac{M_2 \times 9 \times 12}{42}$$
$$72 = \frac{18 M_2}{7} \implies M_2 = \frac{72 \times 7}{18} = 28\text{ men}$$
$$\text{Additional men required} = 28 - 16 = 12$$

questionText: Eighteen persons working 8 hours a day can complete 3 units of work in 10 days. How many days are required by 25 persons to complete 5 units of work working 6 hours a day?
solution:
$$\frac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$$
$$\frac{18 \times 10 \times 8}{3} = \frac{25 \times D_2 \times 6}{5}$$
$$480 = 30 D_2 \implies D_2 = \frac{480}{30} = 16\text{ days}$$

questionText: 18 men can complete $\frac{1}{5}$ of a work in 10 days. How many people are required to complete $\frac{2}{5}$ of the same work in 5 days?
solution:
$$\frac{M_1 D_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2}{W_2}$$
$$\frac{18 \times 10}{1/5} = \frac{M_2 \times 5}{2/5}$$
$$180 \times 5 = \frac{5 M_2}{2/5} \implies 18 \times 10 \times 2 = 5 M_2$$
$$360 = 5 M_2 \implies M_2 = 72\text{ people}$$

questionText: 30 men working 5 hours a day can do work in 18 days. In how many days will 20 men working 7 hours a day do the same work?
Twelve men working for 9 hours a day complete a piece of work in 24 days. In how many days can 8 men working for 12 hours a day complete the same piece of work?
solution:
$$M_1 D_1 H_1 = M_2 D_2 H_2$$
$$12 \times 24 \times 9 = 8 \times D_2 \times 12$$
$$24 \times 9 = 8 D_2 \implies 216 = 8 D_2 \implies D_2 = 27\text{ days}$$

questionText: Eight laborers working 10 hours a day completed a work in 18 days. If only 5 laborers are working, then in how many hours a day should they work to finish the work in 24 days?
solution:
$$M_1 D_1 H_1 = M_2 D_2 H_2$$
$$8 \times 18 \times 10 = 5 \times 24 \times H_2$$
$$1440 = 120 H_2 \implies H_2 = \frac{1440}{120} = 12\text{ hours/day}$$

questionText: 30 persons working 10 hours a day can do 5 units of work in 12 days. How many people are required to do 8 units of that work in 16 days if they work for 8 hours a day?
solution:
$$\frac{M_1 D_1 H_1}{W_1} = \frac{M_2 D_2 H_2}{W_2}$$
$$\frac{30 \times 12 \times 10}{5} = \frac{M_2 \times 16 \times 8}{8}$$
$$720 = 16 M_2 \implies M_2 = \frac{720}{16} = 45\text{ people}$$

questionText: A group of 25 tourists consume 5 containers of food in 8 days in a hotel. How many containers will be required for 10 tourists to eat for 16 days?
solution:
$$\frac{T_1 \times D_1}{C_1} = \frac{T_2 \times D_2}{C_2}$$
$$\frac{25 \times 8}{5} = \frac{10 \times 16}{C_2}$$
$$40 = \frac{160}{C_2} \implies C_2 = \frac{160}{40} = 4\text{ containers}$$

questionText: 36 persons can do a work in 10 days, working 6 hours a day. In how many days will 24 persons, working 9 hours a day complete the work?
solution:
$$M_1 D_1 H_1 = M_2 D_2 H_2$$
$$36 \times 10 \times 6 = 24 \times D_2 \times 9$$
$$2160 = 216 D_2 \implies D_2 = \frac{2160}{216} = 10\text{ days}$$

questionText: 36 equally efficient workers can paint 25 identical walls in 48 days. In how many days can 45 such workers paint 60 such walls?
100 workers working 8 hours a day can dig a canal 2000 metres long in 25 days. Find the number of workers required to dig a similar canal of 2800 metres long in 32 days working 5 hours a day.
In a camp of 70 boys, there are food provisions for 36 days. If 50 boys join the camp, then how many days will the provisions last?
solution:
$$\text{Total provisions} = 70 \times 36 = 2520\text{ boy-days}$$
$$\text{New strength} = 70 + 50 = 120\text{ boys}$$
$$\text{Days lasting} = \frac{2520}{120} = 21\text{ days}$$

questionText: In an army camp, there is food provision for 500 cadets for 25 days. If 125 more persons join the army camp on the first day itself, then for how many days will the provision last?
solution:
$$\text{Total provisions} = 500 \times 25 = 12500\text{ cadet-days}$$
$$\text{New strength} = 500 + 125 = 625\text{ cadets}$$
$$\text{Days lasting} = \frac{12500}{625} = 20\text{ days}$$

questionText: 30 men can complete a work in 12 days. After 6 days, 24 more men joined them. How many days will they now take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
$$\text{Remaining work for 30 men} = 30 \times (12 - 6) = 180\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Total men working} = 30 + 24 = 54\text{ men}$$
$$\text{Days required} = \frac{180}{54} = \frac{10}{3} = 3\frac{1}{3}\text{ days}$$

questionText: 10 men can do a work in 25 days. After 12 days of work, 3 more men were engaged to finish the work. The number of days required to complete the remaining work is:
solution:
$$\text{Remaining work for 10 men} = 10 \times (25 - 12) = 130\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Total men engaged} = 10 + 3 = 13\text{ men}$$
$$\text{Days required for remaining work} = \frac{130}{13} = 10\text{ days}$$

questionText: Working for 10 hours per day, 6 men can build a wall in a certain number of days. By working for how many hours per day can 12 men build the wall in the same days?
solution:
$$M_1 H_1 D = M_2 H_2 D$$
$$6 \times 10 = 12 \times H_2$$
$$60 = 12 H_2 \implies H_2 = \frac{60}{12} = 5\text{ hours}$$

questionText: A group of men committed to completing a task in 20 days. The work was completed in 40 days because 5 workers did not come for work. Determine the number of men who originally agreed to do the work?
solution:
$$\text{Let the original number of men be } M.$$
$$M \times 20 = (M - 5) \times 40$$
$$20M = 40M - 200 \implies 20M = 200 \implies M = 10\text{ men}$$

questionText: A work can be completed by N men in 15 days. 5 men leave the work after 3 days. The remaining work was completed in 18 days. What is the value of N?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 15N$$
$$15N = 3N + (N - 5) \times 18$$
$$15N = 3N + 18N - 90$$
$$15N = 21N - 90 \implies 6N = 90 \implies N = 15$$

questionText: To finish a work in 12 days, 8 workers are engaged. After 2 days, due to some urgency, the work is to be finished in next 2 days. How many more workers are to be engaged now to finish it on time?
solution:
$$\text{Remaining work} = 8 \times (12 - 2) = 80\text{ worker-days}$$
$$\text{Workers required to finish in 2 days} = \frac{80}{2} = 40\text{ workers}$$
$$\text{Additional workers to be engaged} = 40 - 8 = 32$$

questionText: 18 workers can complete a piece of work in 96 days. They start working together and after 26 days 10 more workers join them. In how many days in all will the work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Remaining work after 26 days} = 18 \times (96 - 26) = 18 \times 70 = 1260\text{ worker-days}$$
$$\text{Total workers now} = 18 + 10 = 28\text{ workers}$$
$$\text{Time required for remaining work} = \frac{1260}{28} = 45\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days in all} = 26 + 45 = 71\text{ days}$$

questionText: A hostel had food provision for 300 students for a month. After 20 days, 50 students left the hostel. How long would the remaining food last? (1 month = 30 days)
solution:
$$\text{Remaining provision} = 300 \times (30 - 20) = 3000\text{ student-days}$$
$$\text{Remaining students} = 300 - 50 = 250\text{ students}$$
$$\text{Days lasting} = \frac{3000}{250} = 12\text{ days}$$

questionText: A work can be finished by 8 men in 10 days working 6 hours a day or same can be finished by 20 qualified workers in 6 days working 8 hours a day. 2 men and 4 qualified workers work simultaneously 10 hours a day, the work will be finished in ____ days.
solution:
$$8M \times 10 \times 6 = 20Q \times 6 \times 8 \implies 480M = 960Q \implies 1M = 2Q$$
$$\text{Total work} = 480 \times 2 = 960\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Hourly rate of } 2M + 4Q = 2(2) + 4(1) = 8\text{ units/hour}$$
$$\text{Daily rate (10 hours/day)} = 8 \times 10 = 80\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Days required} = \frac{960}{80} = 12\text{ days}$$

questionText: In an office, 75 employees can finish a project in 60 days. After few days, 15 employees left the job and the project was completed in 65 days. After how many days did the 15 employees leave?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 75 \times 60 = 4500\text{ employee-days}$$
$$\text{Let they leave after } x \text{ days.}$$
$$75x + (75 - 15)(65 - x) = 4500$$
$$75x + 60(65 - x) = 4500$$
$$75x + 3900 - 60x = 4500$$
$$15x = 600 \implies x = 40\text{ days}$$

questionText: $(N + 18)$ persons, each working for 7.5 hours a day, can complete 48% of a work in 20 days. $(N + 12)$ persons can complete the remaining work in 30 days, if each of them works for 6.5 hours per day. Determine the value of N.
20 men can complete a piece of work in 40 days, and 40 women can do the same work in 60 days. If 10 men and 20 women work together, then in how many days will the work be completed?
solution:
$$20M \times 40 = 40W \times 60 \implies 800M = 2400W \implies 1M = 3W$$
$$\text{Total work} = 800 \times 3 = 2400\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 10M + 20W = 10(3) + 20(1) = 50\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{2400}{50} = 48\text{ days}$$

questionText: 15 men can complete a work in 25 days, and 25 women can complete the same work in 40 days. If all the 15 men and 25 women work together, in how many days will the work get completed?
solution:
$$\text{Daily rate of 15 men} = \frac{1}{25},\quad \text{Daily rate of 25 women} = \frac{1}{40}$$
$$\text{Combined daily rate} = \frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{40} = \frac{8 + 5}{200} = \frac{13}{200}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{200}{13} = 15\frac{5}{13}\text{ days}$$

questionText: 15 men and 25 women can complete a piece of work in 9.6 days. If 16 women can complete the same work in 27 days, find the number of days in which 16 men can complete the same work.
solution:
$$(15M + 25W) \times 9.6 = 16W \times 27$$
$$144M + 240W = 432W \implies 144M = 192W \implies 3M = 4W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{4}{3}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 16(3) \times 27 = 1296\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 16 men} = 16 \times 4 = 64\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{1296}{64} = \frac{81}{4} = 20.25\text{ days}$$

questionText: Work done by 8 men is completed in 10 days. The same work can be completed in 12 days when done by 10 women. How many days will it take to complete when 4 men and 4 women are employed to perform the same job?
solution:
$$8M \times 10 = 10W \times 12 \implies 80M = 120W \implies 2M = 3W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 8(3) \times 10 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 4M + 4W = 4(3) + 4(2) = 12 + 8 = 20\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{240}{20} = 12\text{ days}$$

questionText: 10 women can do a work in 6 days and 6 men can do the same work in 5 days. If all these men and women work together, then how many days will they take to finish this work?
solution:
$$\text{Daily rate of 10 women} = \frac{1}{6},\quad \text{Daily rate of 6 men} = \frac{1}{5}$$
$$\text{Combined daily rate} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{11}{30}$$
$$\text{Time taken together} = \frac{30}{11} = 2\frac{8}{11}\text{ days}$$

questionText: 2 men can finish a work in 6 days and 3 women can finish the same work in 4 days. In how many days will the work be finished by 1 man and 2 women, working together every day?
solution:
$$2M \times 6 = 3W \times 4 \implies 12M = 12W \implies 1M = 1W$$
$$\text{Total work} = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 1M + 2W = 1 + 2 = 3\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{12}{3} = 4\text{ days}$$

questionText: 12 men can do a work is 8 days while 4 boys can do it in 40 days. In how many days 9 boys and 3 men together will complete the same work?
solution:
$$12M \times 8 = 4B \times 40 \implies 96M = 160B \implies 3M = 5B \implies \frac{M}{B} = \frac{5}{3}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 96 \times 5 = 480\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 3M + 9B = 3(5) + 9(3) = 15 + 27 = 42\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{480}{42} = \frac{80}{7}\text{ days}$$

questionText: 4 men and 7 women can do a work in 8 days. 7 men and 4 women can do the same work in 5 days. Find the number of days in which 8 women can finish the work?
solution:
$$(4M + 7W) \times 8 = (7M + 4W) \times 5$$
$$32M + 56W = 35M + 20W \implies 3M = 36W \implies 1M = 12W$$
$$\text{Total work} = (4 \times 12 + 7) \times 8 = 55 \times 8 = 440\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 8 women} = 8\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{440}{8} = 55\text{ days}$$

questionText: If 6 women can complete a work in 3 days, and 9 girls can complete the same work in 2 days, then find the time taken to complete the same work by 8 women and 6 girls?
solution:
$$6W \times 3 = 9G \times 2 \implies 18W = 18G \implies 1W = 1G$$
$$\text{Total work} = 18\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 8W + 6G = 8 + 6 = 14\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{18}{14} = \frac{9}{7}\text{ days}$$

questionText: 8 men and 12 women finish a job in 4 days. While 6 men and 14 women in 5 days. In how many days will 20 women finish the job?
solution:
$$(8M + 12W) \times 4 = (6M + 14W) \times 5$$
$$32M + 48W = 30M + 70W \implies 2M = 22W \implies 1M = 11W$$
$$\text{Total work} = (8 \times 11 + 12) \times 4 = 100 \times 4 = 400\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 20 women} = 20\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{400}{20} = 20\text{ days}$$

questionText: Sixteen men can complete a work in 8 days. Eight men and nine women working together can complete the same work in 10 days. In how many days will 20 women complete this work?
solution:
$$16M \times 8 = (8M + 9W) \times 10$$
$$128M = 80M + 90W \implies 48M = 90W \implies 8M = 15W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{15}{8}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 16(15) \times 8 = 1920\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 20 women} = 20 \times 8 = 160\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{1920}{160} = 12\text{ days}$$

questionText: 3 men can finish a work in 10 days, 4 women can finish it in 12 days and 10 qualified workers can finish it in 6 days. In how many days is the work finished by 4 men, 4 women and 4 qualified workers, working together every day?
solution:
$$3M \times 10 = 4W \times 12 = 10Q \times 6 = \text{Total Work}$$
$$30M = 48W = 60Q = 240\text{ units}$$
$$M = 8,\quad W = 5,\quad Q = 4$$
$$\text{Rate of } 4M + 4W + 4Q = 4(8) + 4(5) + 4(4) = 32 + 20 + 16 = 68\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{240}{68} = \frac{60}{17}\text{ days}$$

questionText: 4 men and 8 women complete a job in 10 days and 5 men and 24 women complete the same work in 4 days. In how many days will 1 man and 1 women complete the same work?
solution:
$$(4M + 8W) \times 10 = (5M + 24W) \times 4$$
$$40M + 80W = 20M + 96W \implies 20M = 16W \implies 5M = 4W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{4}{5}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (4 \times 4 + 8 \times 5) \times 10 = 56 \times 10 = 560\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 1M + 1W = 4 + 5 = 9\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{560}{9} = 62\frac{2}{9}\text{ days}$$

questionText: 15 men and 21 women, working together, can do a job in 56 days, while 12 men and 24 women, working together, can do the same job in 64 days. In how many days can the same job be done by 18 men and 24 women, working together?

A man and a woman can finish a work together in half the time taken by a woman and a boy together. A boy can finish the work alone in 20 days and 2 women together can finish it in 30 days. In how many days will the work be finished by 4 men?
solution:
$$\text{Time for 1 boy} = 20\text{ days},\quad \text{Time for 1 woman} = 30 \times 2 = 60\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 60\text{ units} \implies E_B = 3,\quad E_W = 1$$
$$\text{Time taken by woman and boy} = \frac{60}{1 + 3} = 15\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by man and woman} = \frac{15}{2} = 7.5\text{ days}$$
$$E_M + E_W = \frac{60}{7.5} = 8 \implies E_M = 8 - 1 = 7$$
$$\text{Rate of 4 men} = 4 \times 7 = 28\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{60}{28} = \frac{15}{7} \approx 2.14\text{ days}$$

questionText: 4 men's work is equal to 6 women's work, and 4 women's work is equal to 6 boys' work. A boy can finish the work in 60 days. In how many days can the work be finished by a man and a woman together?
solution:
$$4M = 6W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{3}{2} = \frac{9}{6}$$
$$4W = 6B \implies \frac{W}{B} = \frac{3}{2} = \frac{6}{4}$$
$$M : W : B = 9 : 6 : 4$$
$$\text{Total work} = 4 \times 60 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 1M + 1W = 9 + 6 = 15\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{240}{15} = 16\text{ days}$$

questionText: 10 women take 16 days to complete a work which can be completed by 6 men in 8 days. 12 men started working and after 2 days 6 men left, and 5 women joined them. In how many days will the work be completed ?
solution:
$$10W \times 16 = 6M \times 8 \implies 160W = 48M \implies 10W = 3M \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{10}{3}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 6(10) \times 8 = 480\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by 12 men in 2 days} = 12(10) \times 2 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 480 - 240 = 240\text{ units}$$
$$\text{New rate of 6 men and 5 women} = 6(10) + 5(3) = 60 + 15 = 75\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Remaining days} = \frac{240}{75} = \frac{16}{5}\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days to complete work} = 2 + \frac{16}{5} = \frac{26}{5}\text{ days}$$

questionText: 1 man and 4 women can complete a work in $\frac{65}{4}$ days, while 3 men and 4 women can complete it in $\frac{13}{2}$ days. In how many days will 13 women complete the same.
solution:
$$(1M + 4W) \times \frac{65}{4} = (3M + 4W) \times \frac{13}{2}$$
$$\text{Dividing both sides by } \frac{13}{4}: \quad 5(1M + 4W) = 2(3M + 4W)$$
$$5M + 20W = 6M + 8W \implies 1M = 12W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{12}{1}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (12 + 4) \times \frac{65}{4} = 16 \times \frac{65}{4} = 260\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of 13 women} = 13 \times 1 = 13\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{260}{13} = 20\text{ days}$$

questionText: 25 men and 45 women can complete a piece of work in 15 days, while 15 men and 60 women can complete it in 20 days. In how many days can 69 men and 67 women complete the work?
solution:
$$15(25M + 45W) = 20(15M + 60W)$$
$$3(25M + 45W) = 4(15M + 60W)$$
$$75M + 135W = 60M + 240W \implies 15M = 105W \implies 1M = 7W$$
$$\text{Total work} = (25 \times 7 + 45) \times 15 = 220 \times 15 = 3300\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 69M + 67W = 69(7) + 67(1) = 483 + 67 = 550\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{3300}{550} = 6\text{ days}$$

questionText: A project can be completed by 2 men and 5 women in 8 days while 4 men and 6 women can complete the same project in 5 days. How many men will be required to complete this project in 4 days?
solution:
$$8(2M + 5W) = 5(4M + 6W)$$
$$16M + 40W = 20M + 30W \implies 4M = 10W \implies 2M = 5W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{5}{2}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (2 \times 5 + 5 \times 2) \times 8 = 20 \times 8 = 160\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required daily work for 4 days} = \frac{160}{4} = 40\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Men required} = \frac{40}{5} = 8\text{ men}$$

questionText: 5 men and 2 boys can do in 30 days as much work as 7 men and 10 boys can do in 15 days. How many boys should join 40 men to do the same work in 4 days?
solution:
$$30(5M + 2B) = 15(7M + 10B)$$
$$2(5M + 2B) = 7M + 10B$$
$$10M + 4B = 7M + 10B \implies 3M = 6B \implies 1M = 2B$$
$$\text{Total work} = (5 \times 2 + 2) \times 30 = 12 \times 30 = 360\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required daily work for 4 days} = \frac{360}{4} = 90\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Work done by 40 men} = 40 \times 2 = 80\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Remaining work for boys} = 90 - 80 = 10\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Boys required} = \frac{10}{1} = 10\text{ boys}$$

questionText: 4 men and 5 women can complete a work in 15 days, whereas 9 men and 6 women can complete it in 10 days. To complete the same work in 7 days, how many women should assist 4 men?
solution:
$$15(4M + 5W) = 10(9M + 6W)$$
$$3(4M + 5W) = 2(9M + 6W)$$
$$12M + 15W = 18M + 12W \implies 6M = 3W \implies 2M = 1W \implies \frac{W}{M} = \frac{2}{1}$$
$$\text{Total work} = (4 \times 1 + 5 \times 2) \times 15 = 14 \times 15 = 210\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required daily work for 7 days} = \frac{210}{7} = 30\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Work done by 4 men} = 4 \times 1 = 4\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Remaining work for women} = 30 - 4 = 26\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Women required} = \frac{26}{2} = 13\text{ women}$$

questionText: Five men can complete a work in 20 days. Ten women can complete the same work in 15 days. Two men and six women started working together. After 5 days, three women left the work and a new man joined the work. The group continued working together till the end of the work. In how many days will they be able to do the remaining work?
solution:
$$5M \times 20 = 10W \times 15 \implies 100M = 150W \implies 2M = 3W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 100 \times 3 = 300\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by 2 men and 6 women in 5 days} = [2(3) + 6(2)] \times 5 = 18 \times 5 = 90\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 300 - 90 = 210\text{ units}$$
$$\text{New group: 3 men and 3 women} \implies \text{Rate} = 3(3) + 3(2) = 15\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time for remaining work} = \frac{210}{15} = 14\text{ days}$$

questionText: 4 men and 6 women can complete a work in 5 days, while 3 men and 4 women can complete it in 7 days. Similar how many men will have to help 25 women to complete $2\frac{1}{2}$ times the work in 5 days?
solution:
$$5(4M + 6W) = 7(3M + 4W)$$
$$20M + 30W = 21M + 28W \implies 1M = 2W \implies \frac{M}{W} = \frac{2}{1}$$
$$\text{Initial total work} = (4 \times 2 + 6 \times 1) \times 5 = 14 \times 5 = 70\text{ units}$$
$$\text{New work to complete} = 2.5 \times 70 = 175\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Required daily rate for 5 days} = \frac{175}{5} = 35\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Rate of 25 women} = 25 \times 1 = 25\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Remaining rate for men} = 35 - 25 = 10\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Men required} = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ men}$$

questionText: If 3 goats or 5 sheep can graze a field in 54 days, then in how many days can 6 goats and 8 sheep graze the same field?
solution:
$$3G = 5S \implies \frac{G}{S} = \frac{5}{3}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 3(5) \times 54 = 810\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 6G + 8S = 6(5) + 8(3) = 30 + 24 = 54\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{810}{54} = 15\text{ days}$$

questionText: If one man or two women or four boys or five girls can finish a work in 39 days, then how many days will one man, one woman, one boy and one girl together take to finish the same work?
solution:
$$1M = 2W = 4B = 5G$$
$$\text{LCM}(1, 2, 4, 5) = 20 \implies M = 20,\quad W = 10,\quad B = 5,\quad G = 4$$
$$\text{Total work} = 20 \times 39 = 780\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 1M + 1W + 1B + 1G = 20 + 10 + 5 + 4 = 39\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{780}{39} = 20\text{ days}$$

questionText: If 8 men or 16 women or 32 boys can do a piece of work in 8 months, then in how many months can 4 men, 4 women and 4 boys together complete the work?
solution:
$$8M = 16W = 32B \implies 1M = 2W = 4B$$
$$\text{Efficiencies: } M = 4,\quad W = 2,\quad B = 1$$
$$\text{Total work} = 8(4) \times 8 = 256\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Rate of } 4M + 4W + 4B = 4(4) + 4(2) + 4(1) = 16 + 8 + 4 = 28\text{ units/month}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = \frac{256}{28} = \frac{64}{7} = 9\frac{1}{7}\text{ months}$$

questionText: The one-day work of 2 men is equal to the one-day work of 4 women or the one-day work of 8 qualified workers. 10 qualified workers can finish a work in 8 days. If a man, a woman and a qualified worker work in the same order on three different days, the work is finished in ____ days.
solution:
$$2M = 4W = 8Q \implies 1M = 2W = 4Q$$
$$\text{Efficiencies: } M = 4,\quad W = 2,\quad Q = 1$$
$$\text{Total work} = 10(1) \times 8 = 80\text{ units}$$
$$\text{In a 3-day cycle (Man, Woman, Worker), work done} = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done in } 11 \times 3 = 33\text{ days} = 11 \times 7 = 77\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 80 - 77 = 3\text{ units, to be done by Man (efficiency 4)}$$
$$\text{Time taken} = 33 + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{135}{4}\text{ days}$$

questionText: A contractor decided to complete a work in 80 days and employed 60 men at the beginning and 20 men additionally after 20 days and got the work completed as per schedule. If he had not employed the additional men, how many extra days would he have needed to complete the work (round off to the nearest integer)?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 60 \times 20 + (60 + 20) \times (80 - 20) = 1200 + 80 \times 60 = 1200 + 4800 = 6000\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Time taken with original 60 men} = \frac{6000}{60} = 100\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Extra days needed} = 100 - 80 = 20\text{ days}$$

questionText: A civil contractor planned to build an over bridge of 3 km distance in 600 days. For this purpose, he employed 90 workers. After 200 days of work, it was observed that only 0.5 km of the bridge was completed. What is the number of extra workers required to complete the work in time?

questionText: 60 men can complete a work in 40 days. They start work together but after every 10 day, 5 men leave the work. In how many days will the work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 60 \times 40 = 2400\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Days 1 to 10: } 60 \times 10 = 600\text{ units (cumulative: 600)}$$
$$\text{Days 11 to 20: } 55 \times 10 = 550\text{ units (cumulative: 1150)}$$
$$\text{Days 21 to 30: } 50 \times 10 = 500\text{ units (cumulative: 1650)}$$
$$\text{Days 31 to 40: } 45 \times 10 = 450\text{ units (cumulative: 2100)}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 2400 - 2100 = 300\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Men available for next stretch} = 40\text{ men}$$
$$\text{Days required} = \frac{300}{40} = 7.5\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 40 + 7.5 = 47.5\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IX: CONCEPT OF AP IN TIME & WORK
questionText: Each one of five men independently can complete a work in 20 days. The work is started by one person. Next day one more person joins and every next day one more person joins. From the fifth day, five persons continued working as a team. In how many days, will the work be completed?
solution:
$$\text{Let rate of 1 person} = 1\text{ unit/day} \implies \text{Total work} = 20\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done in first 4 days} = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 20 - 10 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{From day 5, rate of 5 persons} = 5\text{ units/day}$$
$$\text{Additional days required} = \frac{10}{5} = 2\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total days} = 4 + 2 = 6\text{ days}$$

typeHeader: TYPE - IX: CONCEPT OF AP IN TIME & WORK
questionText: A group of men decided to complete a job in 4 days. However, since 10 men dropped out every day, the job got completed at the end of the 7th day. How many men were there in the beginning?
solution:
$$\text{Let the initial number of men be } M.$$
$$\text{Total work} = 4M$$
$$\text{Work done in 7 days} = M + (M - 10) + (M - 20) + (M - 30) + (M - 40) + (M - 50) + (M - 60)$$
$$= 7M - 210$$
$$7M - 210 = 4M \implies 3M = 210 \implies M = 70\text{ men}$$

questionText: A and B working together can complete the work in d days. Working alone, A takes $(8 + d)$ and B takes $(18 + d)$ days to complete the same work. A works for 4 days, In how many days will B alone complete the remaining work?
solution:
$$d = \sqrt{8 \times 18} = \sqrt{144} = 12\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by A alone} = 8 + 12 = 20\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = 18 + 12 = 30\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(20, 30) = 60\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = 3,\quad E_B = 2$$
$$\text{Work done by A in 4 days} = 3 \times 4 = 12\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work} = 60 - 12 = 48\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Time taken by B alone} = \frac{48}{2} = 24\text{ days}$$

questionText: When A alone does a piece of work, he takes 25 days more than the time taken by A and B to do the work together. On the other hand, B alone takes 16 days more than the time taken by A and B to do the work together. How many days will A and B, working together, take to do the work?
solution:
$$\text{Let the time taken by A and B together be } T\text{ days.}$$
$$T = \sqrt{25 \times 16} = 5 \times 4 = 20\text{ days}$$

questionText: Ten men begin to do a work. But after some days, four of them left the job. As a result, the job that could have been completed in 40 days is completed in 50 days. How many days after the commencement of the work did the four men leave?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = 10 \times 40 = 400\text{ man-days}$$
$$\text{Let 4 men leave after } x \text{ days.}$$
$$10x + (10 - 4)(50 - x) = 400$$
$$10x + 6(50 - x) = 400$$
$$10x + 300 - 6x = 400$$
$$4x = 100 \implies x = 25\text{ days}$$

questionText: A work was finished by L, P and Q together. L and P together finished 50 percent part of the work and P and Q together finished 60 percent part of the work. Who among the three is most efficient?

Four persons, P Q, R, S were engaged for doing a task, with the condition that P; Q; R; S work, respectively, on (Mondays, Thursdays); (Tuesdays, Fridays); (Wednesdays, Saturdays); (Sundays). The task was began on a Monday, and got completed on the 15th day, which was also a Monday. If the efficiencies of P Q, R, S in respect of doing this task were in the proportion $1 : 2 : 3 : 4$, then in how many days could R complete the task, working alone without break?
solution:
$$\text{In 14 days (2 full weeks):}$$
$$\text{P worked } 4\text{ days, Q worked } 4\text{ days, R worked } 4\text{ days, S worked } 2\text{ days.}$$
$$\text{On the 15th day (Monday), P worked 1 more day } \implies P\text{ worked } 5\text{ days total.}$$
$$\text{Total work} = 5(1) + 4(2) + 4(3) + 2(4) = 5 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 33\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Efficiency of R} = 3$$
$$\text{Days taken by R alone} = \frac{33}{3} = 11\text{ days}$$

questionText: A and B undertake a project worth ₹36,000. A alone can do the work in 25 days. They worked together for 5 days. For the next five days, B worked alone. After that, A substituted B and completed the remaining work in 5 days. The share of A in the earnings is:
solution:
$$\text{Total days A worked} = 5 + 5 = 10\text{ days}$$
$$\text{Since A alone completes the work in 25 days, fraction of work done by A} = \frac{10}{25} = \frac{2}{5}$$
$$\text{Share of A} = \frac{2}{5} \times 36000 = ₹14,400$$

questionText: Arin alone can do a piece of work in 6 days and Selvi alone can do the same in 8 days. Arin and Selvi undertook to do it for ₹ 7,200. With the help of Kevin, they completed the work in 3 days. How much is to be paid to Kevin?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(6, 8, 3) = 24\text{ units}$$
$$E_{\text{Arin}} = 4,\quad E_{\text{Selvi}} = 3,\quad E_{\text{Total}} = 8$$
$$E_{\text{Kevin}} = 8 - (4 + 3) = 1$$
$$\text{Kevin's share} = \frac{1}{8} \times 7200 = ₹900$$

questionText: Fifteen persons working 12 hours a day earn ₹18,000 per week. How many rupees will 18 persons working 9 hours a day earn per week?
P and Q can do a work in 12 days and 9 days, respectively. They both worked together and earned ₹63,000. The share of P (in) is:
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies } P : Q = \frac{1}{12} : \frac{1}{9} = 3 : 4$$
$$\text{Share of P} = \frac{3}{3 + 4} \times 63000 = \frac{3}{7} \times 63000 = 27,000$$

questionText: A, B and C can do a work in 10 days, 15 days, and 20 days, respectively. They finished that work together and got ₹2,600 as wages. Find C's wage.
solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies: } A : B : C = \frac{1}{10} : \frac{1}{15} : \frac{1}{20} = 6 : 4 : 3$$
$$\text{Sum of ratio} = 6 + 4 + 3 = 13$$
$$\text{C's wage} = \frac{3}{13} \times 2600 = ₹600$$

questionText: 4 women and 7 men earn a total of ₹ 11,480 in 7 days, while 10 women and 17 men earn a total of ₹ 36,360 in 9 days. How much will 11 women and 9 men together earn (in ₹) in 13 days?
solution:
$$\text{Daily earning of } 4W + 7M = \frac{11480}{7} = 1640$$
$$\text{Daily earning of } 10W + 17M = \frac{36360}{9} = 4040$$
$$\text{Multiplying first equation by 5: } 20W + 35M = 8200$$
$$\text{Multiplying second equation by 2: } 20W + 34M = 8080$$
$$\text{Subtracting: } 1M = 120 \implies W = \frac{1640 - 7(120)}{4} = \frac{800}{4} = 200$$
$$\text{Daily earning of } 11W + 9M = 11(200) + 9(120) = 2200 + 1080 = 3280$$
$$\text{Earning in 13 days} = 3280 \times 13 = ₹42,640$$

questionText: Ashok and Anil undertake to do a piece of work for ₹ 4,500. Ashok alone could do the work in the 8 days and Anil in 12 days. With the assistance of Amar, they finished the work in 4 days. What is the share of Amar?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(8, 12, 4) = 24\text{ units}$$
$$E_{\text{Ashok}} = 3,\quad E_{\text{Anil}} = 2,\quad E_{\text{Combined}} = 6$$
$$E_{\text{Amar}} = 6 - (3 + 2) = 1$$
$$\text{Amar's share} = \frac{1}{6} \times 4500 = ₹750$$

questionText: Anita and Anand can complete a work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. They undertook to complete that work for ₹48,000. With the help of Arun, they completed the work in 6 days. Find the sum of the shares of Anita and Anand (in ₹).
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(12, 18, 6) = 36\text{ units}$$
$$E_{\text{Anita}} = 3,\quad E_{\text{Anand}} = 2,\quad E_{\text{Combined}} = 6$$
$$\text{Combined share of Anita and Anand} = \frac{3 + 2}{6} \times 48000 = \frac{5}{6} \times 48000 = ₹40,000$$

questionText: X, Y and Z can do a piece of work in 4 days, 5 days and 7 days, respectively. They get ₹415 for completing the work. If X, Y and Z have worked together to complete the work, what is X's share?
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies } X : Y : Z = \frac{1}{4} : \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{7} = 35 : 28 : 20$$
$$\text{Sum of parts} = 35 + 28 + 20 = 83$$
$$\text{X's share} = \frac{35}{83} \times 415 = 35 \times 5 = ₹175$$

questionText: Tina alone can do a piece of work in 12 days and Meena alone can do the same work in 15 days. If Tina and Meena undertook to do this work for ₹18,000, then how much amount will Meena get, if they work together?
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies Tina : Meena} = 15 : 12 = 5 : 4$$
$$\text{Sum of parts} = 5 + 4 = 9$$
$$\text{Meena's share} = \frac{4}{9} \times 18000 = ₹8,000$$

questionText: Mohit and Rohit undertook a work for ₹4400. Mohit alone can do that work in 10 days and Rohit alone can do the same work in 15 days. If they work together, then what will be the difference in the amount they receive?
solution:
$$\text{Ratio of efficiencies Mohit : Rohit} = 15 : 10 = 3 : 2$$
$$\text{Sum of parts} = 3 + 2 = 5$$
$$\text{Difference in amount} = \frac{3 - 2}{5} \times 4400 = \frac{1}{5} \times 4400 = ₹880$$

questionText: Rani can do a work in 10 days, Priya can do the same work in 15 days and Guddu can do the same work in 12 days. If they do that work together and they are paid ₹9000, then what is the share of Priya?
solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies Rani : Priya : Guddu} = \frac{1}{10} : \frac{1}{15} : \frac{1}{12} = 6 : 4 : 5$$
$$\text{Sum of parts} = 6 + 4 + 5 = 15$$
$$\text{Priya's share} = \frac{4}{15} \times 9000 = 4 \times 600 = ₹2400$$

questionText: A alone can complete the project in 10 days; B alone can complete it in 20 days while C alone can complete it in 30 days. They together earn ₹ 1,100 for the project. By how much do the total earnings of A and C exceed the earnings of B ?
solution:
$$\text{Efficiencies: } A : B : C = \frac{1}{10} : \frac{1}{20} : \frac{1}{30} = 6 : 3 : 2$$
$$\text{Total parts} = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11$$
$$\text{Parts of }(A + C) - B = (6 + 2) - 3 = 8 - 3 = 5$$
$$\text{Difference in earnings} = \frac{5}{11} \times 1100 = ₹500$$

questionText: A can complete a task in 12 days and B can complete the same task in 18 days. They start working together but A works for only 2 days. The remaining work is completed by B. If the total wage is ₹ 2,400, then what is B's share (in ₹)?
solution:
$$\text{Work done by A in 2 days} = \frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}$$
$$\text{Work done by B} = 1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$$
$$\text{B's share} = \frac{5}{6} \times 2400 = 5 \times 400 = ₹2,000$$

questionText: A, B and C can do a work in 8, 10 and 12 days, respectively. After completing the work together, they received ₹ 5,550. What is the share of B (in ₹) in the amount received?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(8, 10, 12) = 120\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = 15,\quad E_B = 12,\quad E_C = 10$$
$$\text{Total efficiency} = 15 + 12 + 10 = 37$$
$$\text{B's share} = \frac{12}{37} \times 5550 = 12 \times 150 = ₹1,800$$

questionText: A and B worked together and received a total of ₹ 18,000 for 15 days. A's efficiency in the work was 5 times that of B's. The daily wage of A (in ₹) was:
solution:
$$\text{Combined daily wage} = \frac{18000}{15} = 1200$$
$$E_A = 5 E_B \implies \text{Ratio } A : B = 5 : 1$$
$$\text{Daily wage of A} = \frac{5}{6} \times 1200 = ₹1,000$$

questionText: A can do a piece of work in 8 days while B alone can do it in 12 days. They work together for 4 days and the remaining work is completed by C alone in 2 days. They are paid ₹ 7,200 for the completion of the entire work. The earnings of A, B and C, respectively, are:
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(8, 12) = 24\text{ units}$$
$$E_A = 3,\quad E_B = 2$$
$$\text{Work done by A in 4 days} = 4 \times 3 = 12\text{ units} \implies \text{Fraction} = \frac{12}{24} = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Work done by B in 4 days} = 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ units} \implies \text{Fraction} = \frac{8}{24} = \frac{1}{3}$$
$$\text{Work done by C in 2 days} = 24 - (12 + 8) = 4\text{ units} \implies \text{Fraction} = \frac{4}{24} = \frac{1}{6}$$
$$\text{Earnings of A} = \frac{1}{2} \times 7200 = ₹3,600$$
$$\text{Earnings of B} = \frac{1}{3} \times 7200 = ₹2,400$$
$$\text{Earnings of C} = \frac{1}{6} \times 7200 = ₹1,200$$

questionText: Samir and Puneet can complete the same work in 10 days and 15 days respectively. The work was assigned for ₹ 4500. After working together for 3 days Samir and Puneet involved Ashok. The work was completed in total 5 days. What amount (in ₹) was paid to Ashok?
solution:
$$\text{Total work} = \text{LCM}(10, 15) = 30\text{ units}$$
$$E_{\text{Samir}} = 3,\quad E_{\text{Puneet}} = 2$$
$$\text{Samir and Puneet worked for all 5 days.}$$
$$\text{Work done by Samir in 5 days} = 5 \times 3 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Work done by Puneet in 5 days} = 5 \times 2 = 10\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Remaining work completed by Ashok} = 30 - (15 + 10) = 5\text{ units}$$
$$\text{Ashok's share} = \frac{5}{30} \times 4500 = \frac{1}{6} \times 4500 = ₹750$$
